summary.text: A 50-year-old man with chronic ITP (relapsed persistent ITP) had received glucocorticoids, rhTPO, eltrombopag, platelet transfusion, traditional Chinese herbal medicine, IVIG and then glucocorticoids again, with platelet counts repeatedly falling (including to at most 10 and 11 x 10^9/L). Tuberculosis was initially not excluded and later ruled out. Hetrombopag with methylprednisolone taper normalized platelets; gout was treated with diclofenac and platelets fell to 20. Re-increased hetrombopag with danazol gave no significant rise after 1 month.

Study treatment was rituximab, hetrombopag (7.5 mg/day orally) and danazol (already taken). Platelets rose from 8 to 37 x 10^9/L (TTR 2 days; CR in 44 days), stayed 61-143 for 6 months, and fell to 31 at 20 days after hetrombopag discontinuation. DoR was reported as 23 months (23+ in Table 1) with no significant adverse reactions; avatrombopag monotherapy maintained platelets above 100 with a peak of 500. Source timing for the relapse is inconsistent (see ambiguities).

summary.text: A 49-year-old woman with chronic ITP (5-year history) had initial platelets 12 x 10^9/L that normalized with rhTPO and glucocorticoids then decreased. In 2021 she presented with thrombocytopenia and was diagnosed with primary Sjögren syndrome; IVIG and glucocorticoids normalized platelets with maintenance methylprednisolone, tacrolimus and hydroxychloroquine. Platelets stayed normal about 1 year, later fell to 1 x 10^9/L, and rhTPO, IVIG and methylprednisolone did not significantly increase them. Bone marrow showed impaired megakaryocyte maturation with mild iron deficiency.

Study treatment was ripertamab with hetrombopag 7.5 mg/day orally plus glucocorticoids, tacrolimus and hydroxychloroquine (secondary Sjögren syndrome); CR in 9 days with platelets 16 to 110 x 10^9/L, hetrombopag stopped after 4 months, platelets normal with DoR >29 months and no related adverse reactions.

summary.text: A 58-year-old man with acute ITP (2-month history; bone marrow smear with impaired megakaryocyte maturation, karyotypes 46 and XY) was treated with dexamethasone and rhTPO (platelets 82), fell to 4 after stopping, rose to 141 after repeating the protocol, then hetrombopag 2.5 mg/day maintenance; after 1 week platelets were 65 and hetrombopag was raised to 5 mg/day, then 29 with skin petechiae after 1 week.

Study treatment was ripertamab with hetrombopag 5 mg/day orally; CR at 2 days with platelets 28 to 115 x 10^9/L, 146 after ripertamab with hetrombopag reduced to 2.5 mg once daily, platelets remained normal with DoR >12 months and no related adverse reactions.
